an8.86:1.1: I have heard that on one occasion the Blessed One, on a wandering tour among the Kosalans with a large Saṅgha of monks, arrived at a Kosalan brahman village named Icchānaṅgala.
an8.86:1.2: There he stayed in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove.
an8.86:1.3: The brahman householders of Icchānaṅgala heard it said,
an8.86:1.4: “Gotama the contemplative—the son of the Sakyans, having gone forth from the Sakyan clan—on a wandering tour among the Kosalans with a large Saṅgha of monks—has arrived at Icchānaṅgala and is staying in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove.
an8.86:1.5: And of that Master Gotama this fine reputation has spread:
an8.86:1.6: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One, worthy & rightly self-awakened, consummate in clear-knowing & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed, teacher of devas & human beings, awakened, blessed. He makes known—having realized it through direct knowledge—this world with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its royalty & commonfolk; he explains the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end; he expounds the holy life both in its particulars & in its essence, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.
an8.86:1.7: It is good to see such a worthy one.’”
an8.86:2.1: So the brahman householders of Icchānaṅgala, when the night was gone, taking many staple & non-staple foods, went to the gate house of the Icchānaṅgala forest grove. On arrival they stood there making a loud racket, a great racket.
an8.86:2.2: Now at that time Ven. Nāgita was the Blessed One’s attendant.
an8.86:2.3: So the Blessed One addressed Ven. Nāgita:
an8.86:2.4: “Nāgita, what is that loud racket, that great racket, like fishermen with a catch of fish?”
an8.86:2.5: “Lord, those are the brahman householders of Icchānaṅgala standing at the gate house to the Icchānaṅgala forest grove, having brought many staple & non-staple foods for the sake of the Blessed One & the Saṅgha of monks.”
an8.86:2.6: “May I have nothing to do with honor, Nāgita, and honor nothing to do with me.
an8.86:2.7: Whoever cannot obtain at will—without difficulty, without trouble—as I do, the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of self-awakening,
an8.86:2.8: let him consent to this slimy-excrement-pleasure, this torpor-pleasure, this pleasure of gains, offerings, & fame.”
an8.86:3.1: “Lord, let the Blessed One acquiesce (to their offerings) now! Let the One Well-Gone acquiesce now!
an8.86:3.2: Now is the time for the Blessed One’s acquiescence, lord! Now is the time for the Blessed One’s acquiescence, lord!
an8.86:3.3: Wherever the Blessed One will go now, the brahmans of the towns & countryside will be so inclined.
an8.86:3.4: Just as when the rain-devas send rain in fat drops, the waters flow with the incline,
an8.86:3.5: in the same way, wherever the Blessed One will go now, the brahmans of the towns & countryside will be so inclined.
an8.86:3.7: Because such is the Blessed One’s virtue & discernment.”
an8.86:4.1: “May I have nothing to do with honor, Nāgita, and honor nothing to do with me.
an8.86:4.2: Whoever cannot obtain at will—without difficulty, without trouble—as I do, the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of self-awakening,
an8.86:4.3: let him consent to this slimy-excrement-pleasure, this torpor-pleasure, this pleasure of gains, offerings, & fame.
an8.86:5.1: “Even some devas, Nāgita, cannot obtain at will—without difficulty, without trouble—as I do, the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of self-awakening.
an8.86:5.2: When you all live together, assemble together, and live committed to dwelling with a group, the thought occurs:
an8.86:5.3: ‘Surely these venerable ones cannot obtain at will—without difficulty, without trouble—as I do, the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of self-awakening, which is why they live together, assemble together, and live committed to dwelling with a group.’
an8.86:6.1: [1] “There is the case, Nāgita, where I see monks laughing out loud, sporting around, tickling one another with their fingers.
an8.86:6.3: ‘Surely these venerable ones cannot obtain at will—without difficulty, without trouble—as I do, the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of self-awakening,
an8.86:6.4: which is why they are laughing out loud, sporting around, tickling one another with their fingers.’
an8.86:7.1: [2] “Then there is the case where I see monks—having eaten as much as they want, filling their bellies—live committed to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of sensory contacts, the pleasure of torpor.
an8.86:7.3: ‘Surely these venerable ones cannot obtain at will—without difficulty, without trouble—as I do, the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of self-awakening, which is why they—
an8.86:7.4: having eaten as much as they want, filling their bellies—live committed to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of sensory contacts, the pleasure of torpor.
an8.86:8.1: [3] “Then there is the case where I see a monk sitting in concentration in a village dwelling.
an8.86:8.3: ‘Soon a monastery attendant will disturb this venerable one in some way, or a novice will, and rouse him from his concentration.’
an8.86:8.4: And so I am not pleased with that monk’s village-dwelling.
an8.86:9.1: [4] “But then there is the case where I see a monk sitting, nodding, in the wilderness.
an8.86:9.3: ‘Soon this venerable one will dispel his drowsiness & fatigue and attend to the wilderness-perception,1 (his mind) unified.’
an8.86:9.4: And so I am pleased with that monk’s wilderness-dwelling.
an8.86:10.1: [5] “Then there is the case where I see a wilderness monk sitting unconcentrated in the wilderness.
an8.86:10.3: ‘Soon this venerable one will center his unconcentrated mind, or protect his concentrated mind.’
an8.86:10.4: And so I am pleased with that monk’s wilderness-dwelling.
an8.86:11.1: [6] “Then there is the case where I see a wilderness monk sitting in concentration in the wilderness.
an8.86:11.3: ‘Soon this venerable one will release his unreleased mind, or protect his released mind.’
an8.86:11.4: And so I am pleased with that monk’s wilderness-dwelling.
an8.86:12.1: [7] “Then there is the case where I see a village-dwelling monk who receives robes, alms food, shelter, & medicinal requisites for curing the sick.
an8.86:12.2: Receiving, as he likes, those gains, offerings, & fame, he neglects seclusion, he neglects isolated forest & wilderness dwellings.
an8.86:12.3: He makes his living by visiting villages, towns, & cities.
an8.86:12.4: And so I am not pleased with that monk’s village-dwelling.
an8.86:13.1: [8] “Then there is the case where I see a wilderness monk who receives robes, alms food, shelter, & medicinal requisites for curing the sick.
an8.86:13.2: Fending off those gains, offerings, & fame, he doesn’t neglect seclusion, doesn’t neglect isolated forest & wilderness dwellings.
an8.86:13.3: And so I am pleased with that monk’s wilderness-dwelling.3
an8.86:14.1: “But when I am traveling along a road and see no one in front or behind me, at that time I have my ease, even when urinating & defecating.”
